column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, update v131072)

# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive; project Owl, the Tears of the Kingdom engine's file layout), SDK 22.2.8 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2 (Ampere shaders); modules main + subsdk0 (movie) + sdk.
# Packed from a NUP container (scripts/pack_nup.py). Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code).

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on.

# nninitStartup asks SetHeapSize 0x18ce00000 (6.2 GB) with the 9 GB pool, as Mario Kart World. 256 MB in front + 4 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 8 GB heap region: a starting split, to be measured
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
# The fork's steady 30 fps (V17): at 30 fps an iPhone lowers the GPU clock until the work fills most of the frame (log 60: 195 of 300 frames over 33.3 ms, 109 payback steps in 40 s).
# the display link's frame latency 2 at the 30 fps cap: 66 ms from submission to display instead of 33, so a 34-38 ms frame is absorbed while the mean fits
# no payback: a late frame's lost time is let go (the game slows by it, as on the console) instead of a step of 3 vsyncs shown for 2, a half-frame jump in motion on the next frame
# The touch controls' Forest colours: blue A, green B, yellow X / Y, red +, deep green shoulders, bronze D-pad, gold rims, all translucent (DmGamepad.m theme_init)
# FF (the kid-with-sword-remake fork's experimental iPhone build of nxnative main): the iPhone's settings from the fork's X line.
# Render pipelines through Metal 4 on the iPhone, with the pipeline archive made offline for the iPhone 18 Pro's GPU (A20 Pro, g19p): draws start from ready bases instead of
# building their pipelines at their first draw (the fork's X3 and later)
# Frame buffering: each present is copied, so the game's swapchain texture is free at once (the fork's V17, a steady 30 fps)
# Handheld, as an iPhone runs it: the game presents 1920x1080 instead of 2048x1152 docked
# Pool tables give a finalized texture's ID the dummy instead of making its texture again: about 2.5 GB at the house-to-forest change (upstream PR #1393, open)

# The Render scale slider (the fork's V15-touch2): a fixed fraction of the game's base size, from 0.25 (480x270 handheld, marked Potato) to 1.0 (1920x1080); the render-scale stub (patches.py) fixes every value up to 1.0

# The game upscales through a chain: agl_ndsr_vr feature pass, network and blend at the render size, agl_ndsr_vr_light scale to 1920x1080. DM_UPSCALER=metalfx skips the chain for MetalFX (nvn_mtl.m up_chain)
# The game's compute dispatches with no barrier of its between them run side by side (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc): 117 at the start of a frame in Kokiri Forest waited each for the one
# before, 5.7 ms; side by side 3.7 ms, the frame 27.1 -> 24.9 ms (docked, Apple M4 Pro), the picture within run-to-run noise
# amiibo: the game's Game/AmiiboSetting file in three variants (scripts/oot_amiibo_overlay.py into the romfs_overlay folder): the daily limit off, the drop chances doubled, or both
